mainTopic: Cooked and diluted wine, יין נסך, and the rules of גילוי (uncovered drinks)
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a discussion about seals: one seal is enough, because a non-Jew will not bother to forge it in order to swap the wine. A ברייתא then forbids cooked wine and אלונתית of non-Jews, and a source about שבת explains what אלונתית is. רבה and רב יוסף rule that diluted wine is not subject to גילוי and cooked wine is not subject to ניסוך. The גמרא asks whether cooked wine is subject to גילוי, and several sources and stories show that it is not. רב פפא limits the diluted-wine rule to well-diluted wine, and two snake stories test that limit. רב אשי warns that we do not rely on clever answers where life is in danger. רבא then rules that diluted wine is subject to both גילוי and יין נסך, while cooked wine is subject to neither. The amud continues with uncovered water: whether a sleeping person scares snakes away, and whose water רב and שמואל would drink. It then lists wines that are exempt from גילוי, such as sharp, bitter, sweet and קרינא wines. It ends with רבא's rule about souring wine, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: One seal is enough to prevent swapping
steps.stepSummary: The last line of an earlier discussion: one seal is enough to stop a non-Jew from swapping wine, because he will not bother to forge a seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for the worry that the non-Jew will swap the wine: since there is one seal, he will not go to the trouble of forging it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer from the previous discussion. It explains why one seal is enough to guard against the non-Jew swapping the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that a non-Jew might secretly exchange a Jew's wine for his own. A single seal is enough protection, because forging a seal is too much effort for him. So we do not need two seals for this concern.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a discussion that began on the previous page. Do not treat it as the start of a new topic.

phrases.english: As for swapping —
phrases.notes: He means the worry that the non-Jew will secretly trade the Jew's wine for his own.

phrases.english: since there is one seal,
he does not bother to forge it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous page about how many seals are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reasoning about human behavior: a forger will not go to that much trouble
steps.terutzMaskana: One seal is enough to guard against swapping.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids cooked wine and אלונתית of non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that cooked wine and אלונתית belonging to non-Jews are forbidden, but אלונתית in its original form is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Cooked wine and אלונתית of non-Jews are forbidden. אלונתית in its original form is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about kinds of wine drinks belonging to non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooked wine and the spiced drink called אלונתית are forbidden when they belong to non-Jews. But אלונתית that is still in its original form, as it was first prepared, is permitted. The term אלונתית is unclear, so the גמרא will explain it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A drink of old wine, clear water and balsam

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מְבוּשָּׁל וַאֲלוּנְתִּית שֶׁל גּוֹיִם — אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: Cooked wine and אלונתית of non-Jews are forbidden;
אלונתית in its original form is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about wine drinks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooked wine and אלונתית of non-Jews are forbidden; אלונתית in its original form is permitted.

steps.title: What is אלונתית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the drink called אלונתית is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is אלונתית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word אלונתית. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the ruling can be understood, we must know what the drink is. This is a request for a definition, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: And which is it, what is it

phrases.english: And what is אלונתית?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term used in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Defining אלונתית from a ברייתא about שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source about שבת that defines אנומלין as wine, honey and pepper, and אלונתית as old wine, clear water and balsam, made for the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned about שבת: one may make אנומלין but not אלונתית. What is אנומלין and what is אלונתית? אנומלין is wine, honey and pepper. אלונתית is old wine, clear water and balsam, which people make for the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a source from the laws of שבת that defines both drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שבת source names two drinks: אנומלין, which may be made on שבת, and אלונתית, which may not. It then lists the ingredients of each. אלונתית was used after bathing in the bathhouse, and this tells us exactly which drink the ברייתא in step 2 means.

keyTerms.meaning: A drink of wine, honey and pepper

phrases.english: As we learned regarding שבת:
One may make אנומלין, but one may not make אלונתית.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא אֵנוֹמֵלִין וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא אֲלוּנְתִּית?
phrases.english: And what is אנומלין and what is אלונתית?
אנומלין is wine, honey and pepper;

phrases.aramaic: אֲלוּנְתִּית — יַיִן יָשָׁן וּמַיִם צְלוּלִין וַאֲפַרְסְמוֹן,
phrases.english: אלונתית is old wine, clear water and balsam,
which they make for the bathhouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלונתית is a mix of old wine, clear water and balsam, made for use at the bathhouse.
steps.whatToRemember: Cooked wine and אלונתית of non-Jews are forbidden. אלונתית is old wine mixed with clear water and balsam.

steps.title: Diluted wine and גילוי; cooked wine and ניסוך
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף rule that diluted wine is not subject to גילוי, and cooked wine is not subject to ניסוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: Diluted wine is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids. Cooked wine is not subject to the rule of wine used for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two rulings that make certain kinds of wine more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine mixed with water does not become forbidden just because it was left uncovered. Cooked wine does not become forbidden as יין נסך when a non-Jew handles it. Each ruling covers one rule only, which leaves an open question about cooked wine and גילוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule forbidding a drink that was left uncovered
Wine poured for idol worship (יין נסך)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different rules here. גילוי is about wine left uncovered. ניסוך is about wine a non-Jew may have used for idol worship. The ruling about cooked wine covers only ניסוך.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the ruling about cooked wine mentions only ניסוך, the question that follows asks about cooked wine and גילוי.

phrases.english: רבה and רב יוסף both say:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מָזוּג אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי,
phrases.english: Diluted wine is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids;

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מְבוּשָּׁל אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם נִיסּוּךְ.
phrases.english: cooked wine is not subject to the rule of wine for idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement about kinds of wine, connected to the topic of cooked wine in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Diluted wine is not subject to גילוי; cooked wine is not subject to ניסוך.

steps.title: Is cooked wine subject to גילוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether cooked wine becomes forbidden if it was left uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is cooked wine subject to the rule of uncovered liquids, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question. It sets up the answers that come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that cooked wine is free from ניסוך. Now the question is whether cooked wine is also free from גילוי, or whether the rule of uncovered liquids still applies to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מְבוּשָּׁל יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
phrases.english: Is cooked wine subject to the rule of uncovered liquids,
or is it not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case the previous ruling did not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether cooked wine is forbidden when left uncovered.

steps.title: רבי יעקב בר אידי testifies that cooked wine is not subject to גילוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the testimony of רבי יעקב בר אידי that cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יעקב בר אידי testified about cooked wine that it is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב בר אידי testified directly that cooked wine left uncovered is still permitted. This answers the question: cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
רבי יעקב בר אידי testified
about cooked wine
that it is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.

steps.title: The same question raised at a sickbed
steps.stepSummary: Scholars visiting the sick רבי ינאי בר ישמעאל raise the same question about cooked wine and גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי בר ישמעאל became ill. רבי ישמעאל בן זירוד and the Rabbis went to visit him. They sat and asked: Is cooked wine subject to the rule of uncovered liquids, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which the same question comes up again. It is setting up a second source for the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story adds support for the answer already given. The question is exactly the same as in step 6, and the answer in the next step will come from a different chain of authorities.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask about his health, to visit him

phrases.english: רבי ינאי בר ישמעאל became ill;

phrases.aramaic: עַל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן זֵירוּד
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל בן זירוד went in to him
together with the Rabbis, to ask about his health.
They sat, and this question came up among them:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מְבוּשָּׁל, יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
phrases.english: Is cooked wine subject to the rule of uncovered liquids,
or is it not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that repeats the question, as a lead-in to a second source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether cooked wine is subject to גילוי.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ruling: cooked wine is not subject to גילוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בן זירוד quotes ריש לקיש, who quoted רבי חייא, that cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בן זירוד said to them: This is what רבי שמעון בן לקיש said in the name of a great man. Who is he? רבי חייא. Cooked wine is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to the question at the sickbed, quoted through a chain of great teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling goes back to רבי חייא, through ריש לקיש, and is reported by רבי ישמעאל בן זירוד. It agrees with the testimony of רבי יעקב בר אידי. The גמרא briefly stops to tell us who the 'great man' was.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן זֵירוּד:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל בן זירוד said to them:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: So said רבי שמעון בן לקיש
in the name of a great man;
and who is he? רבי חייא:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מְבוּשָּׁל אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי.
phrases.english: Cooked wine is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן זֵירוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cooked wine is not subject to גילוי, in the name of רבי חייא.
steps.raayaObject: That cooked wine is not subject to גילוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא, quoted by ריש לקיש

steps.title: The scholars ask whether they can rely on it
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis ask whether they may rely on this report.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Shall we rely on this?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars ask whether this ruling is solid enough to act on. This sets up the final confirmation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are not arguing with the ruling. They want to know whether it is reliable enough to follow in practice.

phrases.english: They said to him: Shall we rely on this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the ruling just given can be used in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ruling is reliable enough to follow.

steps.title: רבי ינאי confirms: rely on it
steps.stepSummary: The sick רבי ינאי בר ישמעאל signals that they may rely on the ruling, and he takes responsibility for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי בר ישמעאל signaled to them: On me and on my neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The sick רבי ינאי, who apparently could not speak much, gestures that they may fully rely on the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'On me and on my neck' means he takes full responsibility for the ruling. This closes the discussion: cooked wine is not subject to גילוי, and one may follow this in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: On me and on my neck: I take responsibility

steps.whatToRemember: Cooked wine is not subject to ניסוך, and it is also not subject to גילוי. רבה and רב יוסף also said diluted wine is not subject to גילוי, but רבא's final ruling in step 21 disagrees.

phrases.aramaic: מַחְוֵי לְהוּ רַבִּי יַנַּאי בַּר יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: רבי ינאי בר ישמעאל signaled to them:
On me and on my neck.
phrases.notes: He is saying, 'Rely on it; I take the responsibility on myself.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְוֵי לְהוּ רַבִּי יַנַּאי בַּר יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of reliance and closes the discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may rely on the ruling that cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.

steps.title: שמואל tells אבלט that cooked wine is not יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: When cooked wine is served, אבלט pulls his hand back, and שמואל tells him cooked wine cannot become יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל and אבלט were sitting together. Cooked wine was brought to them, and אבלט pulled his hand back. שמואל said to him: The Sages said that cooked wine is not subject to the rule of יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that cooked wine does not become forbidden when a non-Jew touches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבלט held back so his touch would not make the wine forbidden for שמואל. שמואל told him there was no need, because cooked wine is outside the rule of יין נסך. This opens a new set of stories about cooked wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine forbidden because a non-Jew may have poured it as an offering to an idol

phrases.english: Shmuel and Ablet were sitting,
they brought cooked wine before them,
he pulled back his hand,
phrases.notes: This is אבלט, a non-Jew. He pulled back so his touch wouldn't make the wine forbidden for שמואל.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to him:
Behold, they said: cooked wine
is not subject to the rule of libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the conclusion about cooked wine and גילוי, the גמרא brings stories supporting step 5's rulings. This one shows in practice that cooked wine is free from יין נסך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooked wine is not subject to the rule of יין נסך.

steps.title: רבי חייא rules that exposed cooked wine is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's maidservant found cooked wine left uncovered, and רבי חייא told her cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some cooked wine belonging to רבי חייא's maidservant was left uncovered. She came to רבי חייא, and he said to her: The Sages said that cooked wine is not subject to the rule of גילוי.
steps.whatsHappening: Another story, this time showing in practice that uncovered cooked wine may still be drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the ruling the earlier steps reached about גילוי, now as a real case. Wine left uncovered is normally forbidden because a snake may have drunk from it and left venom, but cooked wine is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Exposure: liquid left uncovered, feared to have been poisoned by a snake

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya's maidservant:
a certain cooked wine of hers became uncovered,
she came before Rabbi Chiya,
he said to her:
Behold, they said: cooked wine
is not subject to the rule of exposure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא אִיגַּלִּויי לַהּ הָהוּא חַמְרָא מְבַשְּׁלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story with the same pattern, now about גילוי instead of יין נסך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooked wine is not subject to גילוי.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה rules that exposed diluted wine is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה's attendant found diluted wine uncovered, and רב אדא told him diluted wine is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some diluted wine belonging to רב אדא בר אהבה's attendant was left uncovered. רב אדא said to him: The Sages said that diluted wine is not subject to the rule of גילוי.
steps.whatsHappening: A third story adds a new kind of wine: wine mixed with water is also not subject to גילוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story puts into practice the ruling of רבה and רב יוסף in step 5 that diluted wine is not subject to גילוי. It sets up רב פפא's limitation in the next step about how much water it takes.

keyTerms.meaning: Diluted wine, wine mixed with water

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava's attendant:
diluted wine of his became uncovered,
he said to him:
Behold, they said: diluted wine
is not subject to the rule of exposure.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמָּעֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אִיגַּלִּי לֵיהּ חַמְרָא מְזִיגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 13, showing in practice the diluted-wine ruling of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Diluted wine is not subject to גילוי.

steps.title: רב פפא limits the rule to well-diluted wine
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the exemption applies only to wine with a lot of water; a snake will still drink partly diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We only said this when the wine is well diluted. But wine that is only partly diluted, a snake does drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows the ruling of רב אדא בר אהבה, so only very watery wine is free from גילוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind the exemption is that a snake does not drink diluted wine. רב פפא says that is true only with a lot of water. Wine with just a little water is still dangerous if left uncovered.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a phrase that limits a rule)
Partly diluted, only a little water

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We only said this where it is well diluted,
but partly diluted, it drinks.
phrases.notes: "It" is the snake; the גמרא leaves that word out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דִּמְזִיג טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the diluted-wine ruling from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only well-diluted wine is free from גילוי; partly diluted wine is still subject to it.

steps.title: A story suggests snakes avoid even slightly diluted wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: when רבה בר רב הונא's attendant added just a little water to wine, a snake turned away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a snake really drink partly diluted wine? Once רבה בר רב הונא was traveling on a ship carrying wine, and he saw a snake slithering toward it. He told his attendant: Blind this one's eyes. The attendant threw a little water into the wine, and the snake turned back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's claim with a story where only a little water was enough to send a snake away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said a snake drinks partly diluted wine. In the story, a small amount of water made the snake turn away. That seems to show that even slightly diluted wine does not attract snakes, so it should be free from גילוי.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
Blind his eyes: do something to make him lose interest

phrases.english: And does it drink partly diluted wine?
But wasn't Rabba bar Rav Huna
traveling on a ship,
and he was carrying wine with him,
and he saw a certain snake
that was slithering and coming.
He said to his attendant:
Blind the eyes of this one.
phrases.notes: Just an expression. He means: do something so this snake stops wanting the wine.

phrases.english: He took a little water and threw it into it,
and it turned back!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְזִיג וְלָא מְזִיג מִי שָׁתֵי? וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's limitation from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that a snake drinks partly diluted wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A little water drove a snake away, so snakes seem not to want even slightly diluted wine.

steps.title: A snake won't risk its life for diluted wine, but still drinks it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: a snake risks danger only for strong wine; it still drinks diluted wine when no one is around.
steps.simpleTranslation: For strong, undiluted wine, a snake will risk its life. For diluted wine, it will not risk its life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by explaining what the ship story really proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the ship, people were present, so reaching the wine was dangerous for the snake. It took that risk for strong wine but not once water was added. Wine left uncovered with no one around carries no risk, so a snake would drink even partly diluted wine, and רב פפא's ruling stands.
steps.whatToRemember: So far, רב פפא's limit stands: a snake avoids diluted wine only when reaching it is dangerous. The discussion continues, and רבא's final ruling in step 21 is that diluted wine is subject to גילוי.
steps.confusionAlert: The ship story does not prove that snakes dislike diluted wine. It only shows they won't take a risk for it. Uncovered wine with nobody around is still a concern.

phrases.english: For undiluted wine, it risks its life,
for diluted wine, it does not risk its life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַיָּיא מָסַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ, אַמְּזִיגָא לָא מְסַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ship story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: danger present versus no danger
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The snake turned away because it does not drink diluted wine at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The snake turned away only because it would not risk its life for diluted wine. When unguarded, it still drinks partly diluted wine.

steps.title: A snake that made wine overflow so it could drink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim from step 17 by telling of a snake that worked hard to drink diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that a snake won't risk itself for diluted wine? Once רבי ינאי (some say בר הדיא) was in בי עכבורי with people drinking diluted wine. Some wine was left in a container, and they covered it with a cloth. Then they saw a snake bring water and pour it into the container until it was full, so the wine rose above the cloth, and the snake drank it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 17, which said a snake won't risk danger for diluted wine. It brings a story where a snake went to great effort to drink diluted wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said a snake only takes risks for strong wine. Here a snake worked hard, right near people, to reach wine that was already diluted, and it even added more water. That suggests a snake will go after diluted wine, so diluted wine should be subject to גילוי.

keyTerms.meaning: risked its life, put itself in danger

phrases.english: And for diluted wine it will not risk its life?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יַנַּאי הֲוָה בֵּי עַכְבּוֹרֵי,
phrases.english: But wasn't Rabbi Yannai in Bei Akhborei,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ: בַּר הֶדְיָא הֲוָה בֵּי עַכְבּוֹרֵי,
phrases.english: and some say: it was bar Hadaya who was in Bei Akhborei,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ יָתְבִי וַהֲווֹ קָא שָׁתוּ חַמְרָא מְזִיגָא.
phrases.english: they were sitting and drinking diluted wine.
Some wine was left over for them in the container,
and they tied it closed with a cloth,
and they saw a certain snake
that took water and poured it into the container
until it filled the container,
and the wine rose above the cloth, and it drank!
phrases.notes: The snake couldn't get through the cloth, so it raised the level until the wine came up over the top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 17 that a snake will not risk danger for diluted wine.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 17 that a snake only risks danger for strong wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story shows a snake taking real effort and risk, near people, to drink diluted wine.

steps.title: The snake only drinks wine it diluted itself
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a snake drinks wine that it diluted itself, but not wine that others diluted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: wine the snake diluted itself, it drinks. Wine others diluted, it does not drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the story is a special case, because the snake added the water itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves only that a snake drinks wine it mixed on its own. Wine that people diluted is still something a snake avoids, so by this answer diluted wine would not be subject to גילוי.

phrases.english: They say:
Wine that it diluted itself, it drinks;
wine that others diluted, it does not drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by limiting the story to wine the snake diluted itself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (self-diluted wine is different)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story shows snakes go after any diluted wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Snakes only drink wine they diluted themselves, not wine diluted by people.

steps.title: You can't rely on clever answers when life is in danger
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי (or רב משרשיא) rejects using a neat answer to be lenient where there is danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said, and some say it was רב משרשיא: Are you giving a clever answer when it comes to danger?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on the answer of step 19. He says we can't be lenient based on a clever explanation when someone's life could be at risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 19 may work as logic, but the story still shows a snake drank diluted wine. When danger is involved, we don't rely on a possible answer to allow something risky. So diluted wine should be treated as dangerous.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said,
and some say it was Rav Mesharshiyya:
An answer for a matter of danger?
phrases.notes: He means a clever answer is fine for a question, but you don't use it to allow something that could be deadly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects relying on the תירוץ of step 19 for a lenient ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the answer of step 19 in practice. It does not prove the answer is logically wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In matters of danger we do not rely on a possible answer to be lenient.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule: when life may be at risk, we are strict even if a clever argument could allow it.

steps.title: רבא's final ruling on diluted and cooked wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules: יין מזוג is subject to גילוי and to יין נסך; יין מבושל is subject to neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that diluted wine is subject to the danger of being uncovered, and it can also become forbidden wine of idol worship. Cooked wine is not subject to the danger of being uncovered, and it cannot become forbidden wine of idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final הלכה, settling the back-and-forth from steps 13-20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against רבה and רב יוסף in step 5 and רב אדא בר אהבה's story in step 14, diluted wine is treated like regular wine, both for snakes and for יין נסך. For cooked wine, רבא confirms both earlier rulings: it is not subject to גילוי (steps 7 to 13) and not subject to יין נסך (steps 5 and 12).

keyTerms.meaning: wine offered to idols, or wine forbidden because of that concern
being left uncovered, where a snake may have drunk from it

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: יין מזוג — both גילוי and יין נסך apply. יין מבושל — neither applies.

phrases.english: Rava said: The halacha is

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מָזוּג יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי,
phrases.english: diluted wine is subject to the rule of being uncovered,
and is subject to the rule of libation wine;

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן מְבוּשָּׁל אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי,
phrases.english: cooked wine is not subject to the rule of being uncovered,
and is not subject to the rule of libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final halacha after step 20 rejected being lenient with diluted wine.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יין מזוג is subject to גילוי and יין נסך; יין מבושל is subject to neither.

steps.title: Does a sleeping person scare snakes away?
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה בר טובי tells his attendant that snakes fear a sleeping person, but only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A jug of water belonging to the attendant of רב חלקיה בר טובי was left uncovered while he slept next to it. He came to רב חלקיה בר טובי, who told him: They said, 'the fear of a sleeping person is upon them.' But this is only by day, not at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from uncovered wine to uncovered water. It tells a story where רב חלקיה בר טובי says a sleeping person keeps snakes away, but only in the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that a snake may be too afraid to come near a jug if a person is sleeping beside it. רב חלקיה limits this to daytime, so at night the water would still be a problem. The גמרא is setting up its response in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the fear of a sleeping person is upon them (the snakes)

phrases.english: The attendant of Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi —
a certain jug of water of his was left uncovered,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "his," is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and he was sleeping next to it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִלְקִיָּה בַּר טוֹבִי,
phrases.english: He came to Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi,
he said to him: They have said,
"The fear of a sleeping person is upon them,"
and this applies only by day,
but at night, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: uncovered water and whether a sleeping person protects it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Snakes fear a sleeping person, but only during the day.

steps.title: A sleeping person does not protect the water at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea completely: day or night, we don't say snakes fear a sleeping person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There is no difference between day and night. We never say 'the fear of a sleeping person is upon them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב חלקיה's rule from step 22. A sleeping person does not keep snakes away, by day or by night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 allowed relying on a sleeping person during the day. The גמרא removes that leniency completely. Uncovered water near a sleeping person is still a danger at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so, a rejection

steps.whatToRemember: A sleeping person does not protect uncovered water from snakes, not by day and not by night.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't take רב חלקיה's daytime rule as the הלכה. The גמרא rejects it with וְלָא הִיא.

phrases.english: But it is not so;

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא בִּימָמָא וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּלֵילְיָא,
phrases.english: there is no difference by day and no difference at night,
we do not say "the fear of a sleeping person is upon them."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, לָא שְׁנָא בִּימָמָא וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּלֵילְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the daytime leniency stated in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the rule that a sleeping person protects uncovered water, by day and by night.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Snakes are not actually scared off by a sleeping person, so there is no basis for the leniency.

steps.title: רב avoids water from a non-Jew's house but drinks from a widow's
steps.stepSummary: רב would not drink water from an ארמאה's house because they are not careful about גילוי. He did drink from a widow's house, because she keeps up her late husband's habits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would not drink water from a non-Jew's house. He said: they are not careful about leaving drinks uncovered. He would drink from a widow's house. He said: she keeps her husband's ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us whose water רב was willing to drink, and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether we can trust a household to keep water covered. רב says a non-Jew does not follow the הלכה of גילוי, but a widow keeps the careful habits her husband had.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquid left uncovered, which a snake may have drunk from and poisoned

phrases.english: Rav would not drink [water] from the house of an Aramean,
he said: They are not careful about exposure.
From the house of a widow he would drink,
he said: She holds on to her husband's ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב לָא שָׁתֵי מַיָּא מִבֵּי אֲרַמָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of snakes and a sleeping person, the גמרא turns to whose water is safe to drink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: avoid a non-Jew's water, because they are not careful about גילוי. A widow's water is fine, because she keeps her husband's habits.

steps.title: שמואל holds the opposite of רב
steps.stepSummary: שמואל would not drink from a widow's house, because without a husband to fear she may not cover the water. He would drink from a non-Jew's house, because even if they ignore גילוי they care about cleanliness.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל would not drink water from a widow's house. He said: she no longer has a husband to be afraid of, so she does not cover the water. But he would drink from a non-Jew's house. Even if they do not care about the הלכה of uncovered water, they do care about cleanliness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's practice, which is the exact reverse of רב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל looks at what actually makes people cover water. A widow no longer has anyone checking on her. A non-Jew covers water for hygiene, so the water ends up protected even without any halachic reason.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two up. רב trusts the widow and not the non-Jew. שמואל trusts the non-Jew and not the widow.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל לָא שָׁתֵי מַיָּא מִבֵּי אַרְמַלְתָּא,
phrases.english: Shmuel would not drink water from the house of a widow,
he said: She does not have the fear of a husband,
and so she does not cover the water.
But from the house of an Aramean he would drink.
Granted that they are not particular about exposure,
they are at least particular about cleanliness.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל לָא שָׁתֵי מַיָּא מִבֵּי אַרְמַלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's practice, which is the reverse of רב's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: avoid a widow's water, because she has no husband to fear. A non-Jew's water is fine, because they cover it for cleanliness.

steps.title: A second version: שמואל drinks from neither house
steps.stepSummary: A different version says רב avoided the non-Jew's water but drank the widow's, while שמואל drank from neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב would not drink water from a non-Jew's house, but he would drink from a widow's house. שמואל would not drink water from either one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another tradition of what רב and שמואל did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב's practice stays the same. Only שמואל changes: he is stricter and trusts neither household. The reasoning about cleanliness does not appear here.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב לָא שָׁתֵי מַיָּא מִבֵּי אֲרַמָּאָה,
phrases.english: Rav would not drink water from the house of an Aramean,
but from the house of a widow he would drink.
Shmuel would not drink water,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִבֵּי אֲרַמָּאָה וְלָא מִבֵּי אַרְמַלְתָּא.
phrases.english: neither from the house of an Aramean nor from the house of a widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second tradition that changes שמואל's practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רב avoids a non-Jew's water but drinks a widow's, and שמואל avoids both.
steps.whatToRemember: רב always avoids the non-Jew's water and drinks the widow's. The two versions disagree only about שמואל: in the first he drinks the non-Jew's water, in the second he avoids both houses.

steps.title: Three wines that are exempt from exposure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that sharp, bitter, and sweet wine are not subject to גילוי. The גמרא then names the actual drinks he means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: there are three wines that do not have the problem of being left uncovered: sharp, bitter, and sweet. Sharp is a harsh wine strong enough to crack its jug. Bitter is ירנקא. Sweet is a sweetened wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: a list of three wines that do not need to be watched for גילוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was whose drinks we can trust. Now it is which drinks need no worry at all. The idea is that a snake does not drink these unusual wines. The גמרא explains each of the three words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
There are three wines
that are not subject to exposure,
and these are they: sharp, bitter, sweet.
Sharp: harsh tila that cracks the jugs,
Bitter: yarneka,
Sweet: sweetened wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ יֵינוֹת הֵן, וְאֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whose drinks are trusted to which wines are exempt from גילוי altogether.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharp, bitter, and sweet wines are not subject to גילוי.

steps.title: רב חמא explains the three wines as fine wines
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא teaches that the three wines are high-quality drinks: wine with peppers, wine with wormwood, and מי בארג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא teaches it as referring to fine wines: sharp is wine with peppers, bitter is wine with wormwood, sweet is מי בארג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the same three words, sharp, bitter, and sweet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations agree that the three wines are exempt. They disagree only about which drinks the words mean. In the first explanation they are poor wines; רב חמא says they are fine, special drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: In the sense of high quality

phrases.english: Rav Chama teaches it as fine wines:
Sharp: wine with peppers,
Bitter: wormwood wine,
Sweet: mei barg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the three wines in רבי יהושע בן לוי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three exempt wines are wine with peppers, wormwood wine, and מי בארג.

steps.title: קרינא is not subject to גילוי
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש adds another wine: קרינא is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: קרינא does not have the problem of being left uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a drink to the list of things exempt from גילוי. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is one more exempt wine, but the word קרינא is unclear. The גמרא will next ask what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of wine, defined in the next steps

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
Karina is not subject to exposure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another wine to the exempt list.

steps.title: What is קרינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word קרינא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is קרינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about the meaning of a word. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we can use ריש לקיש's rule, we need to know which drink he means.

phrases.english: What is karina?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word ריש לקיש used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which drink the word קרינא refers to.

steps.title: קרינא is sweet wine from Asia
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that קרינא is a sweet wine that comes from עסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: it is a sweet wine that comes from Asia.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question and tells us what קרינא is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרינא is an imported sweet wine. Because it comes from far away, the snakes here are not used to it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Sweet wine that comes from Asia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: חַמְרָא חַלְיָא דְּאָתֵי מֵעַסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what קרינא is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קרינא is a sweet wine imported from עסיא.

steps.title: In its home region קרינא is subject to גילוי
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the exemption: where קרינא is made it is the ordinary local wine, so there it is subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: in its own place it is subject to the problem of being left uncovered. Why? There it is the wine of the region.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to ריש לקיש's rule, which applies only away from where קרינא is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption depends on whether the wine is unfamiliar. Where קרינא is the everyday local wine, snakes are used to it, so the normal rule of גילוי applies. It is still the same wine; only the outcome changes by location.

keyTerms.meaning: In its own place, where it comes from
The ordinary local wine of the region

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being exempt from גילוי can depend on where you are, not only on what kind of wine it is.

phrases.english: Rava says:
And in its place it is subject to exposure.
What is the reason?
It is the wine of the region.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits ריש לקיש's exemption for קרינא to places other than where it is made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where קרינא is the local wine, it is subject to גילוי.

steps.title: Wine that has begun to sour, for the first three days
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that wine which has started to sour is still subject to גילוי and to יין נסך for the first three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this wine that has gone sour, for up to three days it is subject to the problem of being left uncovered and to the prohibition of libation wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a new rule about wine that is turning sour. The rule continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first three days, souring wine is still treated as real wine. It must be guarded from snakes, and a non-Jew's touch can make it forbidden as יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: Has gone sour, has started to turn
Wine forbidden because it may have been used, or touched, for idol worship

phrases.english: Rava said:
This wine that has soured,
until three days

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי וּמִשּׁוּם יֵין נֶסֶךְ,
phrases.english: it is subject to exposure and to libation wine,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי חַמְרָא דְּאַקְרֵים, עַד תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another kind of wine whose status might be in doubt: wine that is turning sour.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the first three days of souring, wine is still subject to both גילוי and יין נסך.
